verses.1: One who loves discipline loves knowledge, but one who hates reproof is a fool.
verses.2: A person who finds favor is better than one who seeks to please the Lord, but a schemer is condemned.
verses.3: No one is established through wickedness, but the roots of the righteous remain firm.
verses.4: A woman of valor is a crown to her husband, but a woman who brings shame is like rot in her own flesh.
verses.5: The plans of the righteous produce justice, but the schemes of the wicked are deceit.
verses.6: The words of the wicked are traps of blood, but the mouth of the upright delivers them.
verses.7: When the wicked are turned away, they vanish, but the house of the righteous stands.
verses.8: A person will be praised according to their wisdom, but a heart devoid of understanding will be despised.
verses.9: Better is a poor man who has his own servant than a fool who boasts of wealth and lacks food.
verses.10: The righteous know the soul of their animals, but the mercy of the wicked is cruel.
verses.11: One who tills their land will be satisfied with food, but the soul of the lazy is a wasteland.
verses.12: The wicked desire what is unjust, but the root of the righteous brings forth fruit.
verses.13: With the sin of their words, the wicked are ensnared, but the righteous escape from trouble.
verses.14: From the fruit of a person’s mouth, their life is filled with good, and the reward of their hands will return to them.
verses.15: A fool’s way seems right in their own eyes, but the one who listens to counsel is wise.
verses.16: A fool reveals their anger on the same day, but a wise person conceals disgrace.
verses.17: One who declares loyalty speaks what is just, but a witness of lies is a deceiver.
verses.18: There are words like the pricks of a sword, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.
verses.19: A truthful tongue endures forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.
verses.20: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but those who plan peace are filled with joy.
verses.21: No evil will befall the righteous, but the wicked are filled with evil.
verses.22: The Lord detests lying lips, but He delights in those who act faithfully.
verses.23: A discerning person guards knowledge, but the heart of fools reveals folly.
verses.24: The hand of the diligent rules, but the lazy will be made a slave.
verses.25: A troubled heart weighs down a person, but a good word brings joy.
verses.26: The righteous are more precious than a friend, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin.
verses.27: A lazy hand does not achieve its aim, but the wealth of a diligent person is precious.
verses.28: In the path of righteousness is life, but the way of the wicked leads to death.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 4: "a crown to her husband" and "rot in her own flesh" reflect the metaphorical structure in the Hebrew.  
- v. 11: "a wasteland" (Hebrew רֵיקִים) is a poetic way to render "emptiness" or "futility" in the context of laziness.  
- v. 26: The Greek version adds "will pursue evil" in the second clause, but the Hebrew only says "their way leads to ruin," which is reflected in the translation.  
- v. 28: The final couplet echoes the structure of Proverbs 11:19 and is rendered to preserve that symmetry in meaning and tone.
